The test image shows a soybean stem split open longitudinally. Key observations:
- Dark brown/reddish-brown internal pith discoloration
- White/cream outer cortex remains intact
- This internal browning pattern is hallmark of Brown Stem Rot

Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference shows BSR's foliar phase (interveinal chlorosis/necrosis). The test image shows the complementary stem phase: internal pith browning with white outer cortex — both are classic Brown Stem Rot presentations. The split stem with dark brown pith and intact white cortex is the definitive diagnostic feature for Brown Stem Rot (*Cadophora gregata*), distinguishing it from SDS (which has white pith when split) and Phytophthora (which browns the outer cortex, not just pith).
